I think this course is very fundamental and focuses on truly important topics that we need to learn. However, the exams often seem unbalanced. While half of the questions are based on what has been shown to us, the other half tends to cover aspects that were either barely mentioned or not discussed at all. Additionally, there is usually one question that is a classic problem found online. One or two questions are often unclear in terms of what they are asking or the methods required, as not all details are provided. For the midterm, I think the time limit could have been a bit longer.
It sometimes feels like the goal of the course is not truly focused on learning but rather on making it easy to lose points. A common issue in CS courses is that past exam questions are never directly shared with students. At best, a few questions might be solved briefly during class, but they avoid sharing them directly, likely because some questions could reappear in future exams. This approach can be frustrating.
When I pointed out a logical issue in the midterm, it was not taken very seriously, but I believe understanding the logic behind questions is important. Since the number of students in this course is small, we were given two very difficult assignments, reportedly because the average scores tend to be high. I think these decisions are not very reasonable and cause the course to deviate from its primary purpose.
